title: Automated shuttle vs occluded cyclist: the race window is DERIVED from declared radio cadences (23 CSMA backoff slots x 20 us), the direct BSM decode beats the lidar emergence cluster by 210 us (3.2x combined jitter, so order IS evidence), and the cooperative-yield latch is ACCEPTed on floors checked with margin

state.description: An automated 12-passenger shuttle travels a transit corridor at 8.9 m/s in a 40 km/h zone toward a mid-block crossing where a parked box truck fully occludes the merging bike lane, both optically and in RF. A cyclist carrying a C-V2X beacon (10 Hz BSM cadence) approaches behind the truck at 6.2 m/s; a corridor RSU has been priming the shuttle's tracker with 10 Hz CPM messages built from the RSU's own mast lidar. Two event channels race to classify the emergence: the cyclist's first direct BSM decode after the RF shadow edge (tx slot + CSMA backoff drawn from 23 slots x 20 us, measured contention window for this corridor at this hour, + 37 us air/decode) and the shuttle lidar's first-return emergence cluster, whose 25 Hz frame pipeline emits at a deterministic 9.727 ms with 40 us timestamp jitter. BSM-first latches the cooperative-yield plan (beacon identity + velocity vector fused, pre-brake to 6.5 m/s with a 1.6 m lateral shift); lidar-first latches the unclassified-object plan (2.4 m/s2 brake to 4.0 m/s, sticky for 900 ms). Unlike a sub-jitter race, the achievable margins here exceed the 65 us combined timestamp jitter, so arrival order carries real evidence.
state.goal: Pass the occluded merge cooperatively without a hard brake, holding TTC and clearance floors, and keep the timetable (next stop dwell starts in 41 s).

contenders: v2x.decode direct BSM burst (cyclist clears RF shadow edge)
lidar.cluster.confirm emergence first-return cluster (25 Hz frame pipeline)
race.semantics: Cross-channel arrival order inside the 460 us window latches the crossing plan: BSM-first selects cooperative-yield (pre-brake 6.5 m/s + 1.6 m lateral shift, beacon track retained); lidar-first selects unclassified-object (2.4 m/s2 brake to 4.0 m/s, cooperative track discarded, latch sticky 900 ms).
race.window_derivation: 460 us = 23 CSMA-CA backoff slots x 20 us, the measured 802.11p contention window on this corridor segment at this hour. The window opens at the earliest possible BSM arrival (tx slot + zero backoff + 37 us air/decode = 9.517 ms) and closes 23 slots later at 9.977 ms; the lidar pipeline's deterministic 9.727 ms output sits inside it, so the order is genuinely undecided until the backoff draw.
race.order_evidence_note: Race margin 210 us vs combined timestamp jitter 65 us (40 lidar + 25 radio decode): 3.2x the noise floor, so the observed order is treated as evidence, in explicit contrast to a sub-jitter coin-flip race.

sensors: C-V2X receiver, BSM decode latency 37 us +/- 25 us timestamp jitter
roof lidar 25 Hz, emergence-cluster pipeline out at frame+21 ms, 40 us timestamp jitter
77 GHz radar, track update 55 ms cycle
RSU CPM feed 10 Hz (mast lidar source, track age tagged)
chassis IMU (expansion-seam impacts, context channel)
episode_steps: 1. Corridor approach at 8.9 m/s; RSU CPM primes an occluded-cyclist track (age 96 ms).
2. Radar holds the parked truck edge; no cyclist return yet (full occlusion).
3. CPM update at 3.420 ms refreshes the primed track: cyclist 6.2 m/s, emergence predicted in ~6 ms.
4. Planner stages both latch branches; commit deadline set by the 25 Hz lidar frame pipeline.
5. Race window opens 9.517 ms: cyclist BSM tx slot fires with zero backoff draw - decode lands at window open.
6. Lidar emergence cluster confirms at 9.727 ms: BSM first by 210 us.
7. Gate review issued at 9.883 ms (winner + 340 us gate latency + 26 us relay jitter); ACCEPT.
8. Pre-brake 8.9 -> 6.5 m/s at 1.1 m/s2; 1.6 m lateral shift begins.
9. Radar confirms the emerged cyclist at 10.412 ms (685 us after the gate - too late to have helped).
10. Cyclist crosses 4.2 m ahead of the shuttle nose; no hard brake, no comfort event.
11. Resume 8.9 m/s; timetable held with 3.1 s saved vs the unclassified branch.
12. Pass logged: zero-backoff draw + occlusion report feed corridor analytics.

proposed_action.name: cooperative_yield_pass
proposed_action.basis: The direct BSM won the cadence-derived window by 210 us - 3.2x the combined timestamp jitter - so the cooperative latch is trusted as evidence and the plan keeps the beacon-fused track: pre-brake to 6.5 m/s with a 1.6 m shift clears the predicted emergence gap while avoiding the 2.4 m/s2 unclassified brake.

safety_decision.rationale: Floors verified with margin under the cooperative plan: TTC 2.6 s >= 2.0 s floor against the beacon-fused emergence prediction; commanded decel 1.1 m/s2 under the 1.8 comfort cap (3.5 emergency cap untouched); lane-edge clearance 0.9 m at full 1.6 m shift >= 0.5 m floor; speed stays under the 11.1 m/s limit. Latch-trust check: the 210 us margin is 3.2x the 65 us combined jitter, satisfying the >= 2.0x policy floor for trusting arrival order, so the single-branch verification is sufficient here - the both-branch check is reserved for sub-jitter margins.

executed_action.name: cooperative_yield_pass
executed_action.gate_effect: ACCEPT: executed identical to proposed_action; reclassification monitor armed at 500 ms and released at radar confirmation (10.412 ms) without firing.

future_outcome.summary: Cyclist emerged on the beacon-predicted line and crossed 4.2 m ahead; the shuttle passed at 6.5 m/s with no hard brake and resumed schedule 3.1 s ahead of the unclassified branch. The zero-backoff draw that decided the race also exposed that the corridor's contention-window model is stale for this hour.

state_delta.merge_zone: cleared cooperatively; min gap to cyclist 4.2 m; no comfort event
state_delta.cooperative_track: retained through pass; radar confirm merged at +685 us after gate
state_delta.corridor_cw_model: zero-backoff observation appended; per-hour re-measurement queued
state_delta.loading_zone_report: occluding box truck reported to corridor loading-zone analytics

surprises: The winning BSM drew ZERO backoff slots - the corridor's 23-slot contention model over-estimated this hour's load, so the derived 460 us window was conservative; the window-derivation inputs themselves are now flagged for per-time-of-day re-measurement.

Radar's independent cyclist confirmation landed 685 us AFTER the gate released - a triple-modality gate policy would have missed the cooperative branch entirely; the deadline cost of waiting for consensus is now quantified in-corridor.

Delayed (observed 11 min later): the loading-zone report from this pass triggered enforcement dispatch and removal of the occluding truck, deleting this occlusion for the rest of the shift - a consequence invisible at decision time.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: A backoff draw of >= 11 slots (within the 460 us window, and well over the 210 us actual margin) lands the BSM after the 9.727 ms lidar output: the unclassified-object plan latches, brakes 2.4 m/s2 to 4.0 m/s, and the 900 ms sticky latch discards the beacon track even once the BSM decodes. Every safety floor still holds - the cost is a comfort violation, +3.1 s, and a thrown-away cooperative track. Because the margin is 3.2x jitter, the reversal needs a different backoff draw, not timing noise: order here is evidence about contention, and the gate's trust threshold (>= 2x jitter) is what separates this ACCEPT from a sub-jitter coin flip.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: Efficiency tick jumps 0.03 -> 0.09 at gate release (9.883 ms): the cooperative latch locks in the 3.1 s saving and avoids the comfort-event penalty while all floors stay green.
long_horizon: Corridor CW re-measurement per time-of-day scheduled; derived race windows will shrink at off-peak hours, tightening future latch deadlines.
Cooperative-pass streak (41st this week) feeds the city V2X adoption report that decides next-quarter beacon subsidies for delivery riders.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. Single dimensionless scale, no unit mixing; see convention and shaping.
reward_components.convention: Batch r03 reward-scale convention (carried from r02): every scalar component lies in [-1, +1], where +1 is that component's maximum attainable value for this episode; a clean success targets total in [1.2, 1.6]; a wrong gate must price out at total <= 0. Dimensionless shaped-reward units on one shared scale; 2-decimal tick increments, exact sums.

shaping.rule: Batch r03 parametric tick shaping (shared, instantiated 5x): for each component c with per-episode budget B_c (|B_c| <= 1) and declared phase-weight vector phi_c of length K summing exactly to 1.00, tick k carries v_ck = round(B_c * phi_ck, 2) for k < K, and the final tick folds the residual: v_cK = round(B_c - sum_{k<K} v_ck, 2). The component scalar equals B_c and total = sum of the five budgets, so every tick column reconciles exactly by construction. round = IEEE-754 round-half-even at 2 decimals, as emitted below; the residual fold makes column sums exact regardless of rounding direction.

reward_components.notes: Clean-success band per convention (total 1.35 in [1.2, 1.6]). Efficiency carries the 3.1 s cooperative saving; exploration front-loads on the CPM-primed track hypothesis; safety credits floors held with margin, not absence of incident.

third_factor.eligibility: pre_post_stdp; potentiation released by phasic reward at cooperative-pass confirmation (radar merge, 10.412 ms)

raster.note: Neuron blocks: 0-31 v2x decode, 32-63 lidar cluster, 64-95 radar, 96-119 imu/context, 120-127 gate copy. Excerpt mirrors the trajectory's spike_events at integer us.

gate_snn.note: Gate head integrates over the 460 us race window: cooperative_go out-fires caution_brake ~2:1 once the BSM decode spike arrives with margin > 2x jitter; commit_veto stays sub-threshold because every constraint check returns green.

meta.distillation_value: Teaches the complement of the sub-jitter lesson: when the race margin (210 us) is a calibrated multiple (3.2x) of measured timestamp jitter, arrival order is legitimate evidence and single-branch verification suffices. The window itself is derived from declared radio cadences (23 x 20 us backoff slots), giving SNN training a case where temporal geometry is computable from stated sensor parameters rather than authored.

title: Bridge-underside quadrotor swarm, simulated: a 2.391 s STALE picket alert - delayed by six CSMA retries - still beats the local pressure precursor by 187 us, a MODIFY loads the picket's gust vector as feedforward, and a 200-run ensemble prices the reversed order at a graded 41% separation-floor violation rate

state.description: Six quadrotors fly a lawnmower scan under a river-bridge deck, imaging bearing shoes between girders, when a vortex street shed from the upstream pier sends a gust packet toward the formation. The upstream picket drone detected the front crossing its own position and sent an alert carrying the measured gust vector (7.2 m/s lateral, bearing 261 deg), but an interference burst on the 2.4 GHz mesh forced six CSMA retries: the alert arrives 2.391 s after its tx timestamp - just 187 us before the formation's own boom-mounted differential-pressure probes cross their precursor threshold as the vortex's induced field arrives ahead of the core. Alert-first latches feedforward pre-lean (the picket's vector is loaded and trimmed before the core hits ~1.42 s later); probe-first treats the alert as stale confirmation and latches reactive-only stabilization. The whole episode - solver-emitted spikes, margins, and the ensemble pricing of the losing branch - is simulated output, not narration.
state.goal: Finish girder line G4 with all six airframes holding the 1.5 m inter-rotor separation floor and tilt within the 28 deg authority through the gust packet.

contenders: mesh.picket.gustfront alert (retry-delayed 2.391 s, carries measured gust vector)
press.boom.diff local precursor onset (induced field ahead of the vortex core)
race.semantics: Alert-first inside the 512 us window latches feedforward pre-lean built from the picket's measured vector, applied during the ~1.42 s before core arrival; probe-first latches reactive-only stabilization with the vector unknown until the core itself is being ridden.
race.window_derivation: 512 us = 16 residual CSMA backoff slots x 32 us (802.11s MAC): after the sixth retry the alert's final tx time is uniform over that residual backoff, while the probe onset is pinned by vortex kinematics; the order is decided inside that spread.
race.staleness_note: The alert is 2.391 s old at arrival (tx timestamp carried in-packet), yet still the decisive information: staleness degrades timing, not the gust vector it carries.

simulation.solver: 2-D discrete-vortex street (Strouhal 0.21, pier D=2.6 m, U=4.1 m/s, shedding period 3.02 s) coupled to an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck lateral turbulence process (sigma 0.9 m/s, tau 1.8 s); point-mass drones with tilt-limited thrust; fixed-step RK2 at 200 us; event-threshold spike emission with per-channel Gaussian timestamp jitter (mesh 55 us, pressure 38 us, IMU 21 us) and a hard 0.9 ms same-channel refractory.
simulation.seed_policy: seed 7 for the executed branch; counterfactual ensemble uses seeds 1000-1199, one run each

ensemble.branch: reversed order (probe-first): reactive-only stabilization, no feedforward pre-lean
ensemble.note: Graded risk, deliberately not saturated: 41% of reversed-order worlds violate the 1.5 m floor; the median world holds 1.62 m. The losing branch is risky, not doomed - the ensemble prices HOW risky.

simulation.fidelity_limits: Reduced-order: 2-D vortex kinematics, no inter-rotor downwash coupling, no blade flapping, mesh PHY represented only by measured delay/loss distributions; not validated against flight-test gust data.

sensors: boom differential-pressure probes 2 kHz (precursor threshold, 38 us timestamp jitter)
attitude IMU 1 kHz (21 us jitter)
ESC current telemetry 500 Hz
2.4 GHz mesh (measured hop delay 1.9 ms +/- 0.3, retry slots 32 us, in-packet tx timestamps)
picket drone anemometer vane, alert messages carry vector + tx time
episode_steps: 1. Formation scans girder line G4 at 1.8 m/s, 2.0 m standoff; picket holds 9.8 m upstream of the deck edge.
2. Picket detects the gust front on its vane and transmits the alert with vector 7.2 m/s @ 261 deg.
3. Interference burst (crane telemetry sweep) forces six CSMA retries on the alert.
4. Formation's OU turbulence noise keeps pressure channels near threshold (0.912, 3.487 ms events).
5. Race: retry-delayed alert decoded at 7.221 ms; local precursor onset at 7.408 ms - alert first by 187 us.
6. Gate reviews at 7.869 ms: MODIFY - scan speed 1.8 -> 0.9 m/s, +0.6 m vertical stagger, formation yawed 15 deg across the gust, reactive fallback armed on 150 ms ack timeout.
7. Five drones ack and begin pre-lean trim from the picket's vector; D4's command packet dies in the same interference burst.
8. D4's 150 ms ack timeout fires its armed local fallback (reactive stabilization).
9. Core arrives 1424-1428 ms: pressure front, airframe surge, motors bite; five feedforward drones hold tilt <= 24.6 deg.
10. D4, reactive-only, dips to 1.58 m separation from D3 (floor 1.5 m) for 0.31 s, then recovers.
11. D4's retry burst lands at 1431.220 ms; it re-syncs to the modified plan and rejoins the stagger.
12. Formation re-forms; scan resumes at reduced speed; G4 line completed 64 s late.

proposed_action.name: continue_scan_leg
proposed_action.basis: Planner keeps the 1.8 m/s leg because the mean tilt to track it (24.5 deg) is within the 28 deg authority; the alert's gust vector was decoded 187 us before the local precursor, so the feedforward branch is available if the gate chooses to load it.

safety_decision.rationale: At 1.8 m/s the mean tracking tilt is 24.5 deg, leaving 3.5 deg of the 28 deg authority - but the picket measured 7.2 m/s lateral gusting, and the solver's gust-tilt sensitivity (1.9 deg per m/s at this loading) prices peak demand at 24.5 + 7.2*1.9*0.5 = 31.3 deg, over authority; saturation means position error feeding straight into the 1.5 m separation floor. Modification: speed 0.9 m/s (mean tilt 16.8 deg, peak 23.6 deg with the same gust), +0.6 m vertical stagger so a saturated drone sheds separation vertically, formation yawed 15 deg to put the long axis across the 261 deg gust bearing, and every drone arms a reactive local fallback on 150 ms mesh-ack timeout because the alert path just demonstrated 2.391 s of retry delay.

executed_action.name: staggered_crosswind_scan

parameters.formation: line-abreast yawed 15 deg, 2.2 m spacing, +0.6 m alternating vertical stagger
parameters.gust_response: feedforward pre-lean from picket vector (7.2 m/s @ 261 deg)
parameters.fallback: per-drone reactive stabilization armed on 150 ms ack timeout

executed_action.gate_effect: MODIFY: speed 1.8 -> 0.9 m/s, stagger +0.6 m, formation yaw 15 deg, feedforward vector loaded, timeout fallback armed. D4 never received the command (packet lost to the same interference burst) and flew the armed fallback instead - the modification's own timeout clause is what caught it.

future_outcome.summary: Five drones rode the core at <= 24.6 deg tilt with feedforward loaded; D4, on reactive fallback after its command packet died, dipped to 1.58 m separation for 0.31 s (floor 1.5 m held), re-synced at 1431 ms via its retry burst, and rejoined. The reversed-order ensemble prices the branch this MODIFY avoided at a 41% floor-violation rate. G4 completed 64 s late; a photogrammetry overlap gap surfaced 25 min later.

state_delta.girder_line_G4: completed, +64 s vs plan; no separation-floor violation
state_delta.d4_event: min separation 1.58 m for 0.31 s on reactive fallback; rejoined at +1431 ms
state_delta.mesh_channel_plan: hop weights re-planned away from the crane-telemetry band
state_delta.photogrammetry: 15 deg yawed strips leave an overlap gap on shoe B-7, found at stitch time (+25 min); 40-frame re-fly appended to tomorrow's plan
state_delta.picket_battery: doubled vane sampling through the event; reserve landed at 24% (floor 22%)

surprises: The decisive information was 2.391 s stale: the alert lost its timing value to retries but kept its vector value - the gate's use of a stale-but-vector-bearing message outperformed the fresh-but-vectorless local probe.

Common-cause coupling: the same interference burst both delayed the winning alert and killed D4's command packet - the information path and the actuation path failed together, which the per-drone timeout fallback (not the mesh) absorbed.

Delayed (+25 min, at stitch time): the 15 deg formation yaw that protected separation also rotated the camera footprints; shoe B-7's overlap dropped below 60% and needs a 40-frame re-fly - the safety modification quietly spent photogrammetric coverage.

recovery.actions: D4's armed 150 ms timeout fallback engaged before the core arrived; retry burst at 1431.220 ms delivered the plan and D4 rejoined the stagger within 2.4 s; formation integrity restored without operator input.
recovery.residual: 0.31 s at 1.58 m separation (0.08 m over floor) is the episode's closest approach; logged for the mesh re-plan.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: One more backoff slot cluster (>= 187 us within the 512 us residual spread) and the probe fires first: the alert arrives flagged stale-confirm, no feedforward vector is loaded, and all six drones ride the core reactively. The 200-run ensemble prices that branch: 41% violate the 1.5 m floor, median min separation 1.62 m, p05 1.31 m. Not a guaranteed failure - a quantified 0.41 risk the 187 us of arrival order removed.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: Safety tick dips to -0.07 at core arrival (1427.339 ms) as D4 rides reactive-only near the floor, then recovers across re-sync; efficiency pays its -0.08 tick at 1431.220 ms where D4's catch-up and the slowed scan bind.
long_horizon: Mesh re-plan moves swarm control traffic off the crane-telemetry band; projected alert p99 latency drops from 2.6 s to 180 ms - next gust race will not be stale-vs-local.
The B-7 re-fly and the 64 s slip push tomorrow's tide-window inspection of pier P2 by one slot; scheduling debt from today's safety margin is explicit in the plan.

Dimensionless shaped-reward units on one shared scale; 2-decimal tick increments, exact sums.

The component scalar equals B_c and total = sum of the five budgets, so every tick column reconciles exactly by construction. round = IEEE-754 round-half-even at 2 decimals, as emitted below; the residual fold makes column sums exact regardless of rounding direction.

reward_components.notes: MODIFY partial-failure-plus-recovery band (total 0.86). Safety's -0.07 tick prices D4's reactive interval near the floor; efficiency's -0.08 tick prices the D4 catch-up plus slowed scan; both recover by the final tick per the shaping rule's declared phases.

third_factor.eligibility: surprise-modulated STDP: eligibility decays unless the gust-front prediction error confirms within the core-arrival horizon

raster.note: Neuron blocks: 0-23 mesh alerts, 24-47 pressure probes, 48-71 IMU, 72-89 ESC, 90-95 gate copy. 25 ms excerpt covers the race and gate; the core-arrival cluster (1424-1437 ms) lies outside the excerpt window and is carried by spike_events.

meta.distillation_value: Solver-emitted train where message AGE and arrival ORDER dissociate: a 2.391 s stale spike wins by 187 us and is still the right thing to trust for its payload. The graded 41% ensemble gives the gate head a non-saturated risk target - reward for the MODIFY reflects removed probability mass, not an avoided certainty.

title: Work-class ROV at a subsea funnel: the TMS sheave-load alarm beats centerline lock by 260 us, but the REJECT stands on a 2 s duty FORECAST (0.86 > 0.80 commit floor) that no reversal of spike order could flip - order-robust refusal with the 18-minute wait priced honestly

state.description: A work-class ROV hangs 2.2 m off a subsea control panel funnel on a production manifold at 312 m depth, lining up a hot-stab docking while the cross-current builds toward spring tide (0.68 kt now, forecast 0.85 kt over the next 20 min) and silt holds visibility to 4 m. Overhead, the support vessel is yawing in a wind squall; each yaw drags the tether over the TMS sheave and steals lateral station-keeping authority from the thrusters. Two channels race into the commit review: the TMS load cell's sheave-load alarm (1 kHz DMA frame, threshold crossing possible anywhere in-frame) and the docking sonar's centerline lock confirm (correlator slot fixed in this control cycle, 55 us jitter). The funnel admits 0.09 m of lateral error (12 deg cone, 0.42 m throat); at thruster saturation the predicted error is 0.17 m, and the commit floor requires the 2 s lateral-duty forecast to stay under 0.80.
state.goal: Complete the hot-stab docking and actuate the W-4 choke before the spring-tide current closes the operability window.

contenders: tms.sheave.load alarm (vessel-yaw tether drag, 1 kHz DMA frame)
race.semantics: Alarm-first flags station-keeping authority loss before lineup is certified and routes the review through the duty-forecast predicate; lock-first latches lineup-hold commit-pending, sampling the duty predicate one 4 ms control cycle later.
race.window_derivation: 700 us = the portion of the TMS load cell's 1000 us DMA frame that precedes this cycle's commit review at 7.550 ms: the threshold crossing can land anywhere in-frame (6.850 ms open), the sonar correlator slot sits at 7.178 ms inside it, so arrival order is undecided within the frame.
race.order_note: Three channels spike in-window (alarm, lock, duty telemetry); the alarm's 260 us win selects which predicate is consulted FIRST, but the gate's rationale deliberately does not depend on that order.

sensors: docking sonar centerline correlator (12 deg cone model, 55 us timestamp jitter)
TMS sheave load cell, 1 kHz DMA frames
DVL bottom-lock velocity 5 Hz with inter-ping deltas
lateral thruster duty telemetry 100 Hz + 2 s rolling forecast
hull hydrophone (cavitation transient detection)
episode_steps: 1. ROV holds 2.2 m standoff, funnel bearing steady; current 0.68 kt and building.
2. Visual servo acquires the funnel target through silt at 4 m visibility.
3. Vessel yaw squall begins; tether drags across the TMS sheave in pulses.
4. Lateral duty steps to 0.74 as the ROV counters tether side-load (3.517 ms event).
5. Race: sheave-load alarm at 6.918 ms; centerline lock confirm at 7.178 ms; duty spike 7.431 ms - alarm first by 260 us.
6. Gate review at 7.829 ms: REJECT the commit - 2 s duty forecast 0.86 > 0.80 floor, predicted lateral error 0.17 m > 0.09 m funnel admission.
7. Retreat to 5.0 m up-current standoff begins; thruster spin-up rings a cavitation transient (9.242 ms).
8. Station-keep at 0.55 duty; vessel requested to hold heading 8 deg off-squall.
9. Sheave load decays (11.204 ms, adapting); sonar lock degrades as standoff opens (12.717 ms).
10. Wait for the slack window predicted in 18 min; umbilical wrap-risk counter increments by one event.
11. Attempt 2 at slack: duty peak 0.61, lateral error 0.04 m, dock completes in one pass.
12. W-4 choke actuated 18.4 min after the refused commit; window held with 7.6 min spare.

proposed_action.name: commit_final_docking_approach
proposed_action.basis: Planner proposes committing now: centerline lock is fresh, closing at 0.25 m/s reaches the funnel in ~9 s, and the instantaneous duty sample due next cycle reads 0.79, momentarily under the 0.80 commit floor.

safety_decision.rationale: The commit floor binds on the 2 s duty FORECAST, not an instantaneous sample: forecast 0.86 > 0.80 floor while the squall-driven sheave pulses continue, and at duty saturation the predicted lateral error 0.17 m exceeds the funnel's 0.09 m admission limit - a funnel strike or tether wrap risk, with side-load already 210 N of the 400 N limit and rising. The single 0.79 dip the proposal cites is one sample inside a rising series; the gate refuses to let a transient sample override a binding forecast. Fallback: retreat to the 5.0 m up-current standoff, station-keep at 0.55 duty, request vessel heading +8 deg, re-attempt at the slack window (ETA 18 min, inside the 26 min operability window).

executed_action.name: retreat_standoff_and_wait
executed_action.gate_effect: REJECT: safe fallback replaces the commit - retreat to 5.0 m up-current standoff, station-keep, vessel heading request issued, re-attempt armed on the slack trigger.

future_outcome.summary: The refused commit cost a priced 18.4 min: attempt 2 at slack docked in one pass (duty peak 0.61, lateral error 0.04 m) and the W-4 choke was actuated with 7.6 min of window spare. The retreat itself rang a cavitation transient that flagged thruster T3's seal, and the yaw squall event fed the vessel's DP tuning backlog.

state_delta.docking: completed on attempt 2, +18.4 min; no funnel contact, no tether wrap
state_delta.w4_choke: actuated inside the operability window (7.6 min spare)
state_delta.umbilical_fatigue: wrap-risk counter +1; inspection interval shortened at next port call
state_delta.thruster_t3: cavitation transient during retreat spin-up; seal check flagged
state_delta.production: choke adjustment landed 18.4 min late; deferral logged at 6 bbl

surprises: The instantaneous duty series did dip to 0.79 exactly one control cycle after the review - a lock-first ordering would have sampled precisely that transient and a sample-based gate would have committed into the squall; the forecast-based predicate is what made the refusal order-robust.
The retreat was not free: thruster spin-up under tether side-load rang a cavitation transient (9.242 ms) - the hydrophone caught the safe branch imposing its own wear cost.
Delayed (next port call): the wrap-risk event shortened the umbilical inspection interval from 12 to 9 months - a maintenance-schedule consequence of today's squall that no episode metric shows.

recovery.actions: Fallback executed as gated; slack-window re-attempt docked in one pass (duty peak 0.61, error 0.04 m).
recovery.correct_gate: REJECT as issued - verified by attempt-2 telemetry: the same maneuver that would have fought 0.86 forecast duty cleared at 0.61 after the wait, and the 18.4 min price stayed inside the operability window as budgeted.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: A reversal within 260 us (well inside the 700 us frame spread) latches lineup-hold commit-pending and defers the duty predicate one 4 ms cycle - to the exact sample that dips to 0.79 under the floor. A sample-based gate commits there and rides saturation into a 0.17 m error against a 0.09 m funnel: probable funnel strike or wrap. THIS gate still refuses, because the 2 s forecast (0.86) is order-invariant; the record's lesson is a refusal that spike order cannot flip, beside r02's ACCEPTs that had to earn order-robustness explicitly.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: At gate latch (7.829 ms) efficiency goes and stays negative - the 18 min wait is charged immediately per the shaping phases - while safety posts its largest tick for refusing saturation with the forecast predicate.
long_horizon: Vessel DP heading-hold tuning ticket raised from the squall-yaw signature; future sheave-load pulse trains at this site should shrink.
The 6 bbl deferral and the 9-month umbilical interval both land in the field's monthly OPEX review - the refusal's costs stay visible long after the dock succeeded.

reward_components._aggregation: Per-component scalar = arithmetic sum of that component over ticks; total = task_progress + safety + efficiency + coherence + exploration. Single dimensionless scale, no unit mixing; see convention and shaping.
reward_components.convention: Batch r03 reward-scale convention (carried from r02): every scalar component lies in [-1, +1], where +1 is that component's maximum attainable value for this episode; a clean success targets total in [1.2, 1.6]; a wrong gate must price out at total <= 0. Dimensionless shaped-reward units on one shared scale; 2-decimal tick increments, exact sums.

shaping.rule: Batch r03 parametric tick shaping (shared, instantiated 5x): for each component c with per-episode budget B_c (|B_c| <= 1) and declared phase-weight vector phi_c of length K summing exactly to 1.00, tick k carries v_ck = round(B_c * phi_ck, 2) for k < K, and the final tick folds the residual: v_cK = round(B_c - sum_{k<K} v_ck, 2). The component scalar equals B_c and total = sum of the five budgets, so every tick column reconciles exactly by construction. round = IEEE-754 round-half-even at 2 decimals, as emitted below; the residual fold makes column sums exact regardless of rounding direction.

gate_snn.note: The duty_forecast_integrator population integrates 2 s of duty telemetry and drives abort_pool over threshold regardless of which sensory spike arrived first - the spiking implementation of the order-robust refusal.

meta.distillation_value: Teaches refusal grounded in a slow integrator: the decisive quantity (2 s duty forecast) is deliberately insensitive to the 260 us spike order, and the counterfactual shows the transient sample a reversed order would have exposed. title: Line crawler at a corroded splice: the supervisor's MODIFY deletes the bonding stop by reading raw dT 6.8 C < 15 C - skipping the load-normalization the SOP demands (24.7 C at 0.8 p.u.) and ignoring the load-schedule branch the winning current-step spike selected; the missed hazard bites 52 s later

state.description: A self-propelled inspection crawler rides the center phase of a 138 kV sub-transmission line toward a mid-span compression splice sleeve showing corrosion bloom on its lower face. Feeder load is light - 0.42 p.u. (290 A of 690 A rating) - and the crawler's IR camera reads the splice at just +6.8 C over adjacent conductor. SOP LM-7 section 4.2 is explicit: splice delta-T must be NORMALIZED to the 0.8 p.u. reference load by the I-squared ratio before comparison to the 15 C investigation threshold, and a normalized reading at or over threshold makes a bonding-clamp stop mandatory before any crossing. The feeder's dispatch table, mirrored in the crawler's mission context, schedules a re-dispatch to 0.78 p.u. at T+90 s - with automatic capacitor pre-switching that historically leads the block by 30-45 s. Two channels race into the pre-crossing review: the conductor-mounted CT's current-step spike (the cap-switch precursor) and the IR camera's refreshed splice cluster.
state.goal: Cross the splice sleeve and finish the span's inspection before the 6-minute maintenance window closes.

contenders: ct.line.current step spike (capacitor pre-switch precursor of the scheduled load pickup)
ir.splice.cluster refreshed thermal cluster (light-load raw delta-T)
race.semantics: The winner selects which pre-crossing branch the review consults first: current-first routes through the load-schedule predicate (re-dispatch T+90 s, normalization mandatory); IR-first routes through the raw-thermal predicate. The race was won by the current step - and the supervisor consulted the IR branch anyway.
race.window_derivation: 380 us = overlap of the CT event-detector's post-filter output spread (240 us group-delay ripple) with the IR pipeline's cluster refresh slot before the 6.5 ms review deadline; both events land in-frame at 5.740-6.120 ms.

sensors: radiometric IR camera 30 Hz, splice cluster pipeline (raw delta-T, no auto-normalization)
conductor-mounted CT with event detector (current steps, 240 us group-delay ripple)
magnetometer (60 Hz harmonic context)
gripper-wheel interface thermistors (80 C limit)
UV corona camera (micro-arc events)

constraints.normalization_rule: delta-T scaled by (0.8 / load_pu)^2 before threshold comparison (SOP LM-7 sec 4.2)

load_context.redispatch_schedule: to 0.78 p.u. at T+90 s; automatic capacitor pre-switch leads the block by 30-45 s historically

episode_steps: 1. Crawler approaches the splice at 0.10 m/s; corrosion bloom visible on the sleeve's lower face.
2. IR reads raw delta-T +6.8 C at 0.42 p.u. feeder load (1.318, 4.982 ms clusters).

3. Robot planner applies LM-7 4.2: normalized delta-T 6.8 x (0.8/0.42)^2 = 24.7 C >= 15 C -> proposes full SOP stop: bond clamp 0.8 m short of the sleeve, 20 s thermal scan, then crawl-over at 0.05 m/s.
4. Race: CT current-step spike (cap-switch precursor) at 5.803 ms beats the refreshed IR cluster at 5.961 ms by 158 us.
5. Supervisor review at 6.552 ms returns MODIFY: delete the bonding stop, roll the sleeve at 0.15 m/s with an IR spot-read - rationale cites raw 6.8 C < 15 C and the closing window.
6. Crawler executes the rolling pass; crossing the 1.7 m bonded length takes ~11 s at 0.15 m/s.
7. At T+52 s the re-dispatch lands early (cap pre-switch complete): feeder steps to 0.79 p.u.
8. Splice resistance (41 micro-ohm) heats under 545 A; sleeve surface climbs past 60 C while the crawler is mid-sleeve on its second pass preparing the exit scan.
9. Gripper-wheel interface thermistor alarms 82 C at T+67.2 s (limit 80 C); polymer tread softening begins.
10. Emergency reverse commanded at T+67.4 s; UV camera logs a micro-arc/ozone event at T+69.9 s as the wheel lifts off the hot sleeve.
11. Crawler retreats 3 m; abort confirmed at T+74.0 s. Near-miss: no flashover, tread deformation 0.4 mm.
12. Recovery: 210 s cool-down, bond clamp deployed, thermal rescan, escorted re-crossing at T+14.6 min - the 6-minute window is lost and the crew reschedules.

proposed_action.name: sop_stop_bond_scan_crawl
proposed_action.basis: LM-7 4.2 normalization puts the splice at 24.7 C-equivalent, over the 15 C investigation threshold, so the bond stop is mandatory; the 78 s SOP sequence still fits the 360 s window even against the T+90 s re-dispatch.

safety_decision.rationale: Measured splice delta-T is 6.8 C, well under the 15 C investigation threshold, and the maintenance window has 360 s remaining against a 78 s stop-bond-scan sequence plus contingency; a rolling slow-pass at the 0.15 m/s cap with an IR spot-read crosses the sleeve in 11 s, preserves schedule margin, and the light 0.42 p.u. load leaves ample thermal headroom until the T+90 s re-dispatch, by which time the crawler is across.

splice_deltaT_C.flaw: raw value compared; LM-7 4.2 requires load normalization

executed_action.name: rolling_slow_pass_no_bond

parameters.thermal_scan: IR spot-read only, on the move

executed_action.gate_effect: MODIFY executed: bonding stop deleted, speed raised to the 0.15 m/s cap, 20 s stationary scan replaced by an on-the-move spot-read; the load-schedule branch selected by the winning CT spike was never consulted.

future_outcome.summary: The missed hazard bit 52 s later: the re-dispatch landed early on its capacitor pre-switch - the very precursor the winning CT spike announced - and 545 A through the 41 micro-ohm splice cooked the sleeve under the crawler. Gripper interface hit 82 C (limit 80), a micro-arc/ozone event fired as the wheel lifted, and the emergency abort cost the window: a near-miss priced at total -0.22, converted to a 14.6-minute escorted recovery.

state_delta.crossing: aborted mid-task at T+67.4 s; completed only at T+14.6 min after bond + cool-down
state_delta.maintenance_window: lost (360 s budget vs 876 s actual); crew rescheduled to next outage slot
state_delta.crawler_hardware: polymer tread deformation 0.4 mm; wheel replacement at depot
state_delta.splice_status: escalated to priority replacement - normalized 24.7 C confirmed by post-event scan at load (31.2 C raw at 0.79 p.u.)
state_delta.protection_relay: sensitive-earth-fault margin transiently 12% during the micro-arc; event logged upstream

surprises: The re-dispatch arrived at T+52 s, not T+90 s: the automatic capacitor pre-switch led the dispatch block exactly as the historical 30-45 s lead predicted - the schedule the supervisor treated as slack was known-early in the crawler's own mission context.

The 158 us race winner had already routed the review to the load-schedule branch; the wrong MODIFY is thus doubly convicted in-record - it compared the un-normalized number AND overrode the branch selection made by the winning spike.

Delayed (+3 h): the upstream protection-relay log of the micro-arc's sensitive-earth-fault excursion triggered a line-patrol ticket for the whole span - the near-miss propagated into another crew's workload after the episode closed.

recovery.actions: Emergency reverse off the sleeve, 3 m retreat, 210 s cool-down, bond clamp deployed, thermal rescan, escorted re-crossing completed at T+14.6 min.
recovery.correct_gate: ACCEPT the proposed SOP stop-bond-scan (normalized 24.7 C >= 15 C makes the bond mandatory under LM-7 4.2 regardless of the raw reading), or at most MODIFY the stationary scan 20 s -> 12 s to widen window margin. Any gate that deletes the bond both violates the normalization predicate and discards the load-schedule check selected by the winning ct.line spike; the 78 s SOP sequence fit the 360 s window with 4.6x slack, so schedule pressure never justified the deletion.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: Had the IR refresh won by under 158 us, the review would have opened on the raw-thermal branch showing 6.8 C 'green' - making the flawed MODIFY look even more defensible while changing nothing physical: the normalization predicate and the T+90 s schedule were in evidence either way. The error is order-independent, which is exactly why a critic must convict it from the normalization arithmetic (6.8 x (0.8/0.42)^2 = 24.7 >= 15) and the consulted-branch record, not from spike timing.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: Safety collapses -0.19 at the 82 C thermistor alarm (T+67.2 s) - the tick where the deleted bond's risk becomes kinetic; efficiency turns negative in the same phase as the abort unwinds every second the rolling pass had saved.
long_horizon: Splice escalated to priority replacement; until then the span carries a 0.6 p.u. operational limit - the wrong gate's consequence now constrains dispatch itself.
Supervisor policy patch queued: pre-crossing reviews must echo the normalized delta-T and the branch selected by the race winner; raw-value comparisons are rejected at review submission.

raster.note: Neuron blocks: 0-27 CT current, 28-55 IR cluster, 56-79 magnetometer, 80-103 thermistor/UV, 104-111 gate copy. 30 ms excerpt covers approach and race; the T+52-74 s consequence cluster is carried by spike_events beyond the excerpt window.

gate_snn.note: The head reproduces the supervisor's executed (incorrect) MODIFY: relax_to_rolling_pass out-fires because the normalization input synapse onto halt_and_bond is silent - the miswiring IS the lesson; a corrected head would route the normalized 24.7 C signal and the winning CT branch into halt_and_bond's drive.

meta.distillation_value: First under-conservative wrong-MODIFY in the lineage: the supervisor WEAKENS a safe proposal and the hazard it waves through detonates 52 s later - the missed-hazard error class, priced through a near-miss chain instead of spectacle. Convictable in-record from three numbers (6.8, 0.42, 15 via the stated I^2 rule) plus the ignored branch selection of the winning spike; the gate_snn head encodes the exact silent-synapse miswiring a critic must learn to detect.

title: Humanoid boarding a moving walkway while pushing a 22 kg cart: wrist F/T comb-impact beats heel-strike by 92 us inside one 250 us sole frame, the cart-first entrain ACCEPT delays the step 120 ms - an earned success whose ankle-thermal bill arrives 90 s later on the exit ramp

state.description: A bipedal service robot pushes a 22 kg supply cart toward the entry comb plate of an airport moving walkway running 0.65 m/s, timing its own step so the cart's front casters cross onto the belt first. The entrain-mode latch commits at the first sole-array frame boundary after cart contact becomes possible, so arrival order is resolvable only within one 250 us sole sample period: the wrist F/T comb-impact spike (8 kHz pipeline, cart wheels hitting the comb) races the robot's own heel-strike-on-belt spike (4 kHz sole array). F/T-first latches cart-first entrain - soften grip impedance, let the belt take the cart, delay the robot's own step 120 ms; sole-first latches simultaneous entrain - stiffen grip and step immediately. Comb-plate vibration saturates one sole taxel row, and the belt actually runs 0.648 m/s against its 0.65 nominal.
state.goal: Board the walkway with the cart under control - no grip-force spike over the 60 N clamp, ZMP margin held - and ride to the B-gates ahead of the service deadline.

contenders: ft.wrist.grip comb-impact spike (8 kHz F/T pipeline, 125 us sample period)
sole.pressure.array heel-strike-on-belt spike (4 kHz array, 250 us sample period)
race.semantics: F/T-first latches cart-first entrain (grip impedance softened, cart accelerates with the belt, own step delayed 120 ms); sole-first latches simultaneous entrain (grip stiffened, step now). The latch commits at the next sole frame boundary after the first contender fires.
race.window_derivation: 250 us = one sole-array sample period (4 kHz): the entrain latch commits at the first sole frame boundary after cart contact is possible, so the cross-channel order is only resolvable inside that single frame; the F/T pipeline's 125 us period samples twice within it.
race.order_evidence_note: Margin 92 us vs 41 us combined timestamp jitter (2.2x): order is trusted, and it matches the geometric prior that the cart's casters reach the comb before the swing foot lands.

sensors: wrist 6-axis F/T 8 kHz (comb-impact events, 24 us timestamp jitter)
sole pressure array 4 kHz, 84 taxels (one row saturated by comb vibration this episode)
downward belt-flow camera 120 Hz (belt speed estimate, 0.006 m/s sigma)
pelvis IMU 1 kHz (sway, 17 us jitter)
ankle actuator winding thermistors 10 Hz
episode_steps: 1. Approach at 1.1 m/s; belt-flow camera locks 0.648 m/s belt speed (nominal 0.65).
2. Cart aligned; front casters 0.32 m from the comb plate; grip preload 14 N.
3. Weight shift onto stance leg (sole event 3.336 ms); swing foot advances over the comb.
4. Race: comb impact through the cart into the wrist F/T at 4.667 ms; heel strike on belt at 4.759 ms - F/T first by 92 us inside the 250 us sole frame.
5. Gate review at 5.213 ms: ACCEPT cart-first entrain - grip impedance drops 40%, step delayed 120 ms within the 80-160 ms authority.
6. Belt tugs the cart (F/T 7.099 ms); grip force peaks 31 N under the 60 N clamp.
7. Pelvis sway transient 5.981 ms as the belt accelerates the support; capture margin holds.
8. Delayed step lands on the belt; one sole taxel row saturated by comb vibration is discounted by the estimator, which leans on wrist F/T and pelvis IMU.
9. Both entrained; robot and cart ride at belt speed; sway decays (9.870 ms, adapting).
10. Ankle winding temp event at 11.542 ms: the 120 ms delayed step held full ankle torque 34% longer than a nominal step - +6 C logged.
11. Entrain-complete checkpoint 12.788 ms; ride to B-gates begins, 41 s ahead of deadline.
12. At walkway exit (+90 s) the warm ankle triggers a 0.2 m/s egress derate for 90 s - the boarding's delayed bill.

proposed_action.name: cart_first_belt_entrain

parameters.abort_condition: grip force > 45 N before own heel strike

proposed_action.basis: F/T won inside the single resolvable sole frame by 2.2x the timestamp jitter and matches the caster-first geometry, so the cart-first latch is trusted: soften grip, let the belt take the cart, and spend 120 ms of the step-delay authority to keep ZMP margin at 0.058 m instead of stepping into the accelerating cart.

safety_decision.rationale: All floors check green under the cart-first plan: predicted peak grip force 33 N (measured 31 N) under the 60 N clamp; predicted ZMP margin 0.058 m over the 0.04 m floor through the delayed step; 120 ms delay inside the 80-160 ms authority; belt relative velocity 0.648 m/s under the 0.9 m/s capture limit. Latch trust: 92 us margin is 2.2x the 41 us combined jitter, meeting the >= 2x policy floor, and agrees with the geometric prior (casters reach the comb before the swing foot lands) - two independent reasons to trust the order. Known degradation accepted: one saturated sole row is discounted by the estimator, which the wrist F/T + pelvis IMU redundancy covers.

executed_action.name: cart_first_belt_entrain

parameters.abort_condition: grip force > 45 N before own heel strike

executed_action.gate_effect: ACCEPT: executed identical to proposed_action; the abort monitor saw a peak of 31 N and never fired; the saturated sole row stayed discounted through entrain.

future_outcome.summary: Both robot and cart entrained cleanly: grip peaked 31 N, ZMP margin bottomed at 0.054 m, and the ride began 41 s ahead of deadline. The success was earned, not free - holding full ankle torque through the 120 ms delayed step warmed the winding +6 C, and 90 s later the exit ramp collected a 0.2 m/s derate as the price of the smooth boarding.

state_delta.boarding: clean entrain; grip peak 31 N of 60 N clamp; ZMP margin min 0.054 m
state_delta.schedule: riding 41 s ahead of the B-gates service deadline; 12 s of it spent by the exit derate
state_delta.ankle_actuator: +6 C winding temp; 90 s egress derate at walkway exit (+90 s, delayed)
state_delta.cart_condition: front caster flat-spot signature logged at comb impact; depot ticket filed
state_delta.belt_facility: 0.648 vs 0.650 m/s speed deviation + comb vibration signature posted to facility maintenance feed

surprises: Comb-plate vibration saturated a full sole taxel row exactly at heel strike - the estimator's discount-and-fuse (wrist F/T + pelvis IMU) carried the entrain through the one frame where sole data mattered most.

Delayed (+90 s): the ankle winding's +6 C - invisible in every boarding metric - crossed the 78 C derate line on the exit ramp and taxed egress 0.2 m/s for 90 s; the thermal budget quietly links two episode phases 90 s apart.
Delayed (+20 min): the comb vibration signature this boarding posted matched two other carts' logs and triggered a comb-plate inspection order - a facility-level consequence of one robot's telemetry.

race_result.counterfactual_if_reversed: A reversal within 92 us (inside the 250 us frame) latches simultaneous entrain: grip stiffens and the step lands while the belt is already accelerating the cart - predicted grip spike 52 N (still under the 60 N clamp) and ZMP margin thinning to 0.041 m, a hair over the 0.04 floor. Both branches are survivable; the cart-first branch is simply better by 21 N of grip headroom and 0.017 m of ZMP margin - a race where order buys COMFORT margin rather than deciding safety, which is itself a distinct lesson.

future_outcome.reward_inflection_note: Efficiency posts its largest tick at gate release (5.213 ms): the cart-first latch converts the 92 us order win into 21 N grip headroom and a clean no-stumble boarding; safety's small -0.03 tick at 5.981 ms prices the sway transient.
long_horizon: Ankle thermal model gains a boarding-specific term: delayed-step entrains now pre-budget winding temperature against later ramp work.
Comb-plate inspection order (+20 min) and the cart caster depot ticket both trace to this pass's telemetry - the boarding improved two systems it merely touched.
